content.value_statement: Architecture documentation often mixes detail levels and confuses stakeholders. This skill guides C4 diagrams with Mermaid syntax, level rules, and review checks.
actual_capabilities: Creates C4 context, container, component, dynamic, and deployment diagrams using Mermaid syntax.
Separates diagram content by C4 abstraction level to avoid mixed views.
Identifies actors, systems, containers, components, and labeled relationships.
Adds technology choices for container and component diagrams when appropriate.
Uses level guidelines and review checks to match diagrams to the intended audience.
Provides Mermaid syntax examples for boundaries, relationships, styling, and common C4 elements.
limitations: It depends on user-provided system details and cannot discover architecture automatically.
It produces documentation guidance, not verified runtime architecture inventory.
Large systems may need several diagrams instead of one complete view.
Code-level diagrams require careful manual review because code changes quickly.

use_cases.title: Plan a New System
use_cases.description: Create context and container diagrams before implementation so teams agree on boundaries and dependencies.

use_cases.title: Explain Existing Architecture
use_cases.description: Turn system knowledge into Mermaid diagrams for onboarding, reviews, and stakeholder discussions.

use_cases.title: Review Technical Designs
use_cases.description: Check whether proposed diagrams use the correct C4 level, labels, descriptions, and technology detail.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Context Diagram
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a high-level system view.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a C4 context diagram for [system]. Users are [actors]. External systems are [dependencies]. Output Mermaid syntax with labeled relationships.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Container Diagram
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request after the context view is known.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a C4 container diagram for [system]. Include web apps, APIs, workers, databases, queues, and external systems. Add technologies and descriptions.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a Component Diagram
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for one important container.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a C4 component diagram for [container]. Show major modules, services, repositories, integrations, and responsibilities. Keep classes out unless critical.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Diagram Levels
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of existing architecture documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these C4 diagrams for mixed abstraction levels, missing labels, unclear boundaries, and audience fit. Recommend specific changes before rewriting them.

output_examples.input: A team asks for a context diagram for an online store with customers, admins, payment, shipping, and email systems.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a Level 1 context view with the store as one system, external systems, people, and labeled relationships.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for a container diagram for an API-backed web and mobile product.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines web, mobile, API, worker, database, cache, queue, and external payment containers with technologies.

output_examples.input: An architect submits a mixed diagram that contains users, databases, modules, and classes together.
output_examples.output: The skill flags the mixed levels and recommends separate context, container, and component diagrams.

best_practices: Start with a context diagram before creating lower-level diagrams.
Keep each diagram at one C4 abstraction level with clear labels and descriptions.
Split complex systems into focused diagrams instead of crowding one view.
anti_patterns: Do not mix users, containers, components, and classes in one diagram.
Do not show implementation details in a context diagram.
Do not create code-level diagrams for simple or frequently changing code.

faq.question: What diagram formats does this skill support?
faq.answer: The guidance centers on Mermaid C4 syntax and also references Structurizr and PlantUML as output format options.

faq.question: Can it create all four C4 levels?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers context, container, component, and code-level diagrams, with stronger guidance for when each level is appropriate.

faq.question: Does it inspect my codebase automatically?
faq.answer: No. It uses information supplied in the prompt and does not include codebase scanning or discovery scripts.

faq.question: When should I use a code-level diagram?
faq.answer: Use it only for critical or complex areas where classes, interfaces, or key abstractions need documentation.

faq.question: Can non-technical stakeholders use the output?
faq.answer: Yes. Context diagrams are intended for broad audiences, while lower levels serve technical stakeholders and developers.

faq.question: How does it reduce architecture diagram mistakes?
faq.answer: It asks for audience, purpose, level selection, descriptions, relationship labels, and checks for mixed abstraction levels.
